Hyundai Motor stock faces weaker sales despite profit growth
sum: Hyundai Motor reported a mixed third quarter on October 29, 2026, with lower revenue and net profit but higher operating profit. The automaker's official results release attributed the operating improvement to favorable exchange rates, cost optimization and a product mix supported by hybrid electric vehicle sales.
Revenue for the July-September period fell 3.4 percent year on year to KRW 45.11 trillion. Net profit, including non-controlling interests, dropped 24.2 percent to KRW 1.93 trillion.

Global wholesale volume declined 11.3 percent to 920,710 vehicles. Hyundai said fewer working days and strike-related production constraints weighed on output, while domestic sales fell 27.2 percent to 131,468 units and sales outside Korea declined 8 percent to 789,242 units.

Operating profit rose 5.5 percent to KRW 2.68 trillion, lifting the operating margin to 5.9 percent. Hybrid electric vehicles accounted for 18.2 percent of global sales, and hybrid volume increased 3.8 percent year on year to 167,414 units.

Electrified vehicles represented 26.7 percent of global sales. Total electrified vehicle sales nevertheless fell 2.7 percent to 245,540 units, while battery-electric vehicle sales declined 9.2 percent to 69,117 units.

Hyundai lowered its 2026 wholesale sales target to 4 million vehicles from 4.16 million. The consolidated operating margin target was reduced to 5.5 to 6.5 percent from 6.3 to 7.3 percent, while the revenue growth target remained at 1 to 2 percent.
The company also reduced its automotive investment plan to KRW 16 trillion from KRW 17.8 trillion. Hyundai maintained its quarterly dividend at KRW 2,500 per common share, according to the release.

FOCUS: Hyundai Motor steps up physical AI push amid Chinese competition, stock slump
sum: UIWANG, South Korea - Seeking to remain competitive against fast-growing Chinese automakers and find new sources of growth amid a sharp retreat in its share price, Hyundai Motor Group is stepping up its push into robotics and physical artificial intelligence.

The move comes as the world's third-largest automotive group faces growing pressure to improve profitability in its conventional carmaking business amid intensifying competition in the global electric vehicle market, particularly from lower-priced Chinese models.
Investors are also questioning when the group's heavy investments in robotics will start to pay off.

Hyundai Motor Co.'s shares more than doubled after its U.S. subsidiary Boston Dynamics unveiled its Atlas humanoid robot at the Consumer Electronics Show in January, reaching a record closing high of 755,000 won (US$565.2) in June.

But the stock has since fallen sharply to near pre-CES levels, closing at 312,000 won Friday, as enthusiasm over robotics has faded amid weak earnings and growing concerns about how soon the technology can turn profitable.

Speculation about a delayed initial public offering of Boston Dynamics has added to the uncertainty. The U.S. robotics company reportedly incurred cumulative losses of around 1.7 trillion won over the past five years.
The sharp drop in stock price shows the challenge facing Hyundai: turning excitement over its robotics business into actual profits while keeping its core automotive operations competitive.

Hyundai Motor Group shares vision for SDF transition with suppliers
sum: Hyundai Motor Group is holding an exhibition of innovative technologies to support the transformation to a Software Defined Factory (SDF). By sharing with its suppliers technologies that use physical AI (artificial intelligence) and more, the group aims to share its future vision of transforming factories into smart factories and to improve production efficiency.

Hyundai Motor and Kia said on the 18th that they will hold the three-day e-Forest Tech Day 2026 from the 19th to the 21st at the Hyundai Motor and Kia Uiwang Research Institute. The event, now in its seventh edition, is a leading technology exhibition where smart factory technologies developed by the Hyundai Motor and Kia Manufacturing Solutions Division and their suppliers are shared.

Some 200 new manufacturing technologies will be showcased at the event under themes including foundational technologies for advancing SDF, autonomous and automated technologies, energy solutions, and future mobility.

The SDF technology section will outline progress in implementing SDF technologies, including quality systems, and present plans for advancing SDF that can be quickly applied at domestic and overseas factories using a standardized technological foundation.

The exhibition will also feature digital twin technology, which runs simulations linked to actual factory equipment in a virtual space identical to the real world, allowing systems to be tested and optimized in advance before problems occur. To implement SDF, Hyundai Motor and Kia are focused on establishing a unified data collection and management system and a common development environment, and laying the groundwork to develop and deploy solutions needed on the manufacturing floor.

The event will also introduce AI agents developed specifically for factory operations, including data retrieval and interpretation, searches for manufacturing know-how, and the preparation of equipment manuals.

The automation technology section will highlight automated assembly and inspection technologies designed to improve work efficiency and manufacturing quality. One technology in this section, tunnel-based visual inspection, places a vehicle inside a tunnel-shaped device and uses 3D simulation to inspect its exterior.

Reliance Industries shares climb 3 percent as Jio Platforms sets IPO price band
sum: Mumbai: Shares of Reliance Industries rallied 3 per cent on Thursday after Jio Platforms Ltd, the digital and telecom arm of the firm, set a price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share for its initial public offering that could raise about Rs 30,213 crore at the top of the range, making it India’s largest.
The blue-chip stock climbed 2.85 per cent to Rs 1,209.50 on the BSE.

The IPO, comprising a fresh issue of up to 27 crore equity shares of Rs 10 face value each, opens for subscription on Wednesday, October 21, and closes on Friday, October 23. Anchor investor bidding is on Monday, October 19, according to regulatory filings by Reliance.

The IPO committee of Jio Platforms’ board approved the band at a meeting on Wednesday, the filing said. Eligible employees bidding in the employee reservation portion will get a discount of Rs 54 per share.
Investors must bid for at least 12 shares and in multiples of 12 thereafter. At the cap price, one lot would cost Rs 13,428.

According to the Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP), the company plans to issue up to 27 crore equity shares with a face value of Rs 10 each. At the cap price, that works out to Rs 30,213 crore, by calculation. That is about 8 per cent above the record set by Hyundai Motor India, whose Rs 27,858.75 crore IPO in 2024 holds the top spot.
It is also roughly 47 per cent above the next largest, Life Insurance Corporation of India’s Rs 20,557.23 crore offering.

sum: Hyundai Motor’s labor union has approved a tentative agreement that includes higher base pay, bonuses and new hiring commitments, concluding months of contentious wage negotiations and strikes.

The carmaker said 19,183 workers, or 61.55 percent of the 31,166 union members who cast ballots in a vote held Monday, voted in favor of this year’s wage agreement between the labor union and the company.

Under the agreement reached last week, Hyundai Motor will raise monthly base pay by 100,000 won ($73) and provide a performance bonus equivalent to 400 percent of monthly salary plus an additional 12.7 million won.

Workers will also receive 15 Hyundai Motor shares and 500,000 won in welfare points. The agreement also includes plans to hire 500 new production workers from the second half of next year through 2028.

The union and management arrived at a tentative agreement on August 25, 111 days after talks began on May 6. With union members ratifying the deal on Monday, this year’s wage negotiations have officially concluded.

The deal came after months of negotiations marked by repeated breakdowns and several strikes that led to production disruptions. The union staged its first full eight-hour strike in a decade, halting 120 hours of production across two shifts this year.
The walkouts have disrupted production of an estimated 55,200 vehicles, resulting in sales losses exceeding 2.3 trillion won, according to industry estimates.

sum: SAN FRANCISCO — Hyundai Motor Co. CEO José Muñoz smiled and nodded as a fellow executive discussed the automaker's "ha-myeon-dwen-da" philosophy during the reveal of its new flagship Genesis GV90 SUV.

The term means "anything is possible" in Korean. It's a mantra for the South Korean automaker that has proved to be true for the company's U.S. ambitions as well as for Muñoz himself, a Spanish-U.S. dual national who is the first non-Korean executive to lead the automaker.

Hyundai has experienced rapid growth in the U.S. so far this decade despite an onslaught of geopolitical changes and a slowing market. And it's hoping to keep that going. The company is ramping up production at a new $7.6 billion plant in Georgia to continue to capture more sales and market share.

"My top three priorities are U-S-A," Muñoz told CNBC during an interview last week after the Genesis reveal. "USA is helping us to really make good progress, not only in the most important market and the most competitive market in the world, but also elsewhere."

Hyundai Motor Group, which includes its namesake vehicles as well as the Kia and luxury Genesis brands, has increased its market share this decade more than any major automaker in the U.S., according to data from Mobility Global.

The group has grown its U.S. market share from 8.4% in 2020 to 11.2% through last year, and its sales have grown 50% over that period, making the South Korean company the fourth best-selling automaker in the country. Its market share is up to 11.8% through the first half of this year, according to auto intelligence firm Mobility Global.

No other major automaker is even close to such market share gains, with most flat to down during that timeframe. Electric vehicle manufacturer Tesla, at an estimated 2.1 percentage point increase in market share, is the only company even close, according to Mobility Global.

items.t: Why three automakers dominate the fast-growing hybrid vehicle market
sum: Just three automakers control the majority of one of the hottest segments in the U.S. car market — and none of them are American companies.

In the first half of 2026, sales of hybrid cars — not long ago considered a bridge to fully electric vehicles — have risen nearly 20% year over year to a record market share of 15.4%, according to the Center for Automotive Research, almost three times the share of pure EVs.
"The only growth we're seeing is in hybrid market share," said Elizabeth Krear, CEO of the Center for Automotive Research. "All other propulsion systems have lost market share year to date."

It has been a boon to the few automakers that invested heavily in the hybrid vehicle market. Toyota, Hyundai Motor Group and Honda together control 86% of it, according to automotive market analysis firm Baum & Associates.
"Consumers want the vehicles. The problem is there are relatively few automakers that offer those vehicles," said Alan Baum, principal at Baum & Associates.

Toyota sold more than 600,000 hybrids in the first half of 2026 between its two brands, Toyota and Lexus. It controls half the market. Toyota's hybrid lineup has pushed overall U.S. volumes closer to top seller General Motors, which has bet big on EVs and has only one hybrid in its U.S. lineup in the Corvette E-Ray. GM told CNBC in an email that "hybrids do have a role in our future product plans."

The other automaker that has invested heavily in hybrids is Hyundai Motor Group, which owns the Hyundai, Genesis and Kia brands. It just barely surpassed Honda in the first half of 2026, according to data from Baum & Associates.

Hyundai slips as EV surge and market shifts reshape South Korea autos
sum: In the first half of this year, Korea's auto industry went through a period of upheaval unlike any before. As Hyundai Motor, which drives the domestic market, showed unusual weakness, Tesla's surge began. With high oil prices caused by the Middle East war and China's BYD joining in, the number of consumers choosing electric vehicles started to rise sharply. The first-half period also marked the initial rollout of the "software-defined vehicle (SDV)," the starting point of future mobility. Here are nine defining scenes that shook the first half.

Hyundai Motor, which leads Korea's auto industry, suffered an unusual slump in the domestic market in the first half of this year. From January to June, Hyundai Motor's domestic sales totaled 316,713 vehicles, down 10.8% from a year earlier. In April, it ceded the No. 1 spot to Kia for the first time in 28 years, and monthly sales have fallen for six straight months since February.

Taking advantage of Hyundai Motor's stumble, Tesla is making big gains. Tesla's first-half sales came to 56,139 vehicles, up 192.2% from the same period a year earlier. Price cuts on key models in December last year and January this year helped. Tesla is running first, ahead of BMW and Mercedes-Benz.
② The end of the chasm in sight… one in four new cars is electric

With China's electric-vehicle maker BYD joining Tesla, domestic EV sales surged explosively. According to Kaizuyu Data Research Institute, new EV registrations in Korea in the first half reached 198,969, up 112.6% from a year earlier. EVs' share of all newly registered cars more than doubled, from 11.1% to 23.3%.

Beyond the price competition among brands, high oil prices caused by the Middle East war also spurred EV expansion. The industry sees the EV "chasm" (a temporary demand lull before mass adoption) as over, with the market entering a growth phase. Kia, for instance, posted a record first-half domestic EV sales tally of 72,078 units this year.

Korea concentrates single-stock ETF bets on Samsung, SK hynix, stoking volatility
sum: Single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds (ETFs) introduced by financial authorities to bring back investment funds that had flowed overseas are becoming a "volatility catalyst" shaking not only Korea's market but also the U.S. market.

Some argue that the issue lies not in the decision to introduce single-stock leveraged ETFs itself, but in a system design that set excessively strict limits on eligible underlying assets. In the United States, a wide range of single-stock leveraged ETFs backed by various stocks are listed, but in Korea the bar was raised so that only products tied to Samsung Electronics and SK hynix could launch, creating a side effect of concentrating investment demand in the two stocks.

With the two stocks already whipsawing under the influence of the semiconductor supercycle, the arrival of leveraged ETFs poured fuel on rapid price swings. The safeguards put in place by the authorities ultimately concentrated investor demand in the two names, laying the groundwork for greater market crowding.

According to Korea Securities Depository (KSD) on the 29th, during the 22 trading days from May 27 to June 26 after the listing of domestic single-stock leveraged ETFs, domestic investors' buy-settlement amount for the Hong Kong–listed SK hynix 2x leveraged ETF was $135,610,000, up 422% from the same period at the start of the year (Jan. 2 to Feb. 2). Over the same period, the buy-settlement amount for the Samsung Electronics 2x leveraged ETF also rose 194% to $73,070,000.

While it is said that investment funds gathered as these stock prices surged and plunged recently, assessments say the policy effect of repatriating overseas investment demand to the domestic market fell short of expectations. The effect on stabilizing the exchange rate was also limited. Recently, the won-dollar rate has remained around 1,540 won, still the highest level since the global financial crisis.

In Korea, trading in leveraged ETFs tracking Samsung Electronics and SK hynix has surged. According to the Korea Exchange (KRX), on the 24th, the trading value of single-stock leveraged and inverse ETFs on Samsung Electronics and SK hynix reached 19.4 trillion won, the highest since listing.
